Les données contenues dans ces supports et documents sont strictement couvertes par le secret professionnel (article 226-13 du code pénal). Conformément aux articles 34 et 35 de la loi du 6 janvier 1978 modifiée relative à l’informatique, aux fichiers et aux libertés, le titulaire du présent accord-cadre s’engage à prendre toutes précautions utiles afin de préserver la sécurité des informations et notamment d’empêcher qu’elles ne soient déformées, endommagées ou communiquées à des personnes non autorisées. Le titulaire s’engage donc à respecter, de façon absolue, les obligations suivantes et à les faire respecter par son personnel, c’est-à-dire notamment à : Ne prendre aucune copie des documents et supports d’informations confiés, à l’exception de celles nécessaires pour les besoins de l’exécution de sa prestation, objet du présent accord-cadre Ne pas utiliser les documents et informations traités à des fins autres que celles spécifiées au présent accord-cadre Ne pas divulgue

deliverables_scope.text: o empower and better resource the Centre to support Ireland’s collective national effort to reverse biodiversity loss and contribute to nature restoration. The primary role of the Centre is to contribute to building the knowledge base on biodiversity and track how it is changing in Ireland. It works to ensure that data and information on Ireland’s biodiversity is more freely available and accessible for use in research, conservation management and decision-making. The National Biodiversity Data Centre is a predominantly publicly funded entity, rather than a public sector body. The Centre formally became a registered charity in November 2025. Requirements This Request for Quotation (RFQ) is a below-threshold competitive procurement process for printing services conducted in line with the National Public Procurement Policy Framework and relevant OGP guidance for goods and services. Quotations are being sought from suitably qualified suppliers for a three-year contract for printing services. This RFQ is being issued to all interested suppliers via public notice. Proposal Submissions should contain information under the following headings: Price (based on a defined representative sample) Technical Capability & Print Quality Sector Understanding & Approach Service, Meetings & Account Management E

Physical Samples and Technical Quality Assessment Tenderers must submit physical production samples demonstrating their capability to deliver printed materials broadly equivalent to the key product types required under this contract, including at a minimum: – A4 booklet (e.g. saddle‑stitched booklet) – Wiro‑bound guidebook – PUR‑bound handbook – Species swatch cards (swatch sets with die‑cut cards and fixings) – A2 posters (folded to A4) and aluminum composite signage (e.g. Dibond) Samples may be existing or recent production work of similar specification; they are not required to be produced specifically for this competition, but must be representative of the tenderer’s current production capability. As part of the evaluation under Criterion Q1 (Technical Capability & Print Quality), the evaluation panel will inspect samples for: – Print quality (colour fidelity, registration, image sharpness, absence of defects); – Finishing quality (trimming, folding, lamination, die‑cutting, drilling, assembly); – Binding integrity (e.g. spine strength for PUR, wire binding quality, durability); – Overall fitness for purpose relative to the specifications described in the pricing basket. Compliance and transparency notes Evaluation methodology: The Contracting Authority will award the contract to the Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT) based on the award criteria, weightings, sub-criteria, scoring bands and price formula set out in this RFQ. The relative importance of each criterion is expressed in the form of maximum marks. No additional criteria will be applied and the published methodology will not be changed after the tender submission deadline. Scoring: All tenders will be evaluated strictly in accordance with the published criteria, sub-criteria, scoring bands and price formula. No additional criteria will be introduced and no changes to the evaluation methodology will be made after the deadline for submission of tenders. Minimum thresholds: Tenderers must achieve the minimum mark specified for each criterion with a minimum threshold. Tenders failing to achieve the minimum mark in any such criterion will be eliminated and will not proceed to award.
